title: The potato trade that looked profitable but wasn't
summary: Agra → Vashi New Mumbai, January 2022: a ₹315 per quintal median price gap on 23 matched days. After modeled costs: −₹65 per quintal on the typical day.
why_selected: Chosen automatically for January 2022: one of AGRINET's documented trade corridors with 23 matched report days.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices; sale matched to the first destination report 1–3 days after transit
caveats: Hypothetical: no actual shipment is claimed.
Modal prices may mix varieties and grades (mostly FAQ).
Costs are survey values and assumptions, not quotes.
OSRM car profile; truck route not verified.

scenes.headline: January 2022
scenes.caption: Agra sits in western Uttar Pradesh's cold-stored potato belt; Vashi supplies Mumbai.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: On 23 matched days, Agra reported a median ₹780 per quintal; Vashi New Mumbai reported ₹1,100 2 days later.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹315/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gross gap was ₹315 per quintal and was positive on 100% of days.

scenes.headline: 1,270 km by road
scenes.caption: Routed road distance 1,270 km (OpenStreetMap car routing, ~15 driving hours). Trucks are slower; we allow 2 days.

scenes.headline: Now add the costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹273/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. Modeled net on the typical (median) day: −₹65 per quintal.

scenes.headline: Stress test
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day becomes −₹189 per quintal.

scenes.headline: Hindsight vs. a real trader
scenes.caption: With perfect hindsight, 4 of 23 days cleared modeled costs. A trader using only reports available on the day would have shipped on 7 of 23 days, averaging ₹4 per quintal; 3 of those shipments lost money.

scenes.headline: The lesson
scenes.caption: The ₹315 gap looked tempting, but on the typical day modeled costs absorbed it. A trader acting on the previous report did average ₹4 per quintal under baseline costs, but −₹123 under the stress test. A gap on a price board is not a margin.

assumptions.value: scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹273/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days

conclusion: The ₹315 gap looked tempting, but on the typical day modeled costs absorbed it. A trader acting on the previous report did average ₹4 per quintal under baseline costs, but −₹123 under the stress test. A gap on a price board is not a margin.

title: The potato storage gamble
summary: Agra potatoes: ₹945 in March 2022, ₹1,480 in October. Break-even storage budget: ₹365 per quintal.
why_selected: Chosen automatically: the yearly harvest-to-autumn storage question at Agra, with 8 earlier seasons to learn from.

evidence.observations: monthly medians of Agra daily modal prices (≥8 reports)
caveats: No cold-storage rent is cited, so no net profit is claimed.
Stored and fresh potatoes may differ in grade.

scenes.headline: March 2022
scenes.caption: Potatoes are harvested in early spring and often held in cold stores in western Uttar Pradesh, which the RBI paper calls the potato belt's key selling point.

scenes.headline: Harvest price
scenes.caption: Agra's March 2022 median: ₹945 per quintal.

scenes.headline: The informed bet
scenes.caption: Using only the 8 earlier years, March→October had averaged +₹408. A rule-following trader would store.

scenes.headline: October 2022
scenes.caption: October median: ₹1,480, a change of +56.6%.

scenes.headline: Shrinkage and interest
scenes.caption: Allowing 7% loss and 12% a year interest for 7 months leaves a storage budget of ₹365 per quintal.

title: The potato trade that looked profitable but wasn't
summary: Agra → Vashi New Mumbai, November 2022: a ₹232 per quintal median price gap on 20 matched days. After modeled costs: −₹232 per quintal on the typical day.
why_selected: Chosen automatically for November 2022: one of AGRINET's documented trade corridors with 20 matched report days.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices; sale matched to the first destination report 1–3 days after transit
caveats: Hypothetical: no actual shipment is claimed.
Modal prices may mix varieties and grades (mostly FAQ).
Costs are survey values and assumptions, not quotes.
OSRM car profile; truck route not verified.

scenes.headline: November 2022
scenes.caption: Agra sits in western Uttar Pradesh's cold-stored potato belt; Vashi supplies Mumbai.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: On 20 matched days, Agra reported a median ₹1,568 per quintal; Vashi New Mumbai reported ₹1,800 2 days later.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹232/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gross gap was ₹232 per quintal and was positive on 100% of days.

scenes.headline: 1,270 km by road
scenes.caption: Routed road distance 1,270 km (OpenStreetMap car routing, ~15 driving hours). Trucks are slower; we allow 2 days.

scenes.headline: Now add the costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹273/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. Modeled net on the typical (median) day: −₹232 per quintal.

scenes.headline: Stress test
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day becomes −₹391 per quintal.

scenes.headline: Hindsight vs. a real trader
scenes.caption: With perfect hindsight, 0 of 20 days cleared modeled costs. A trader using only reports available on the day would have shipped on 2 of 20 days, averaging −₹31 per quintal; 2 of those shipments lost money.

scenes.headline: The lesson
scenes.caption: The ₹232 gap looked tempting, but on the typical day modeled costs absorbed it. A gap on a price board is not a margin.

assumptions.value: scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹273/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days

conclusion: The ₹232 gap looked tempting, but on the typical day modeled costs absorbed it. A gap on a price board is not a margin.
